questions.question: The Bharat Ratna was instituted in which year?
questions.rationale: India's highest civilian award dates from 1954 — the same year as the three Padma awards, which makes 'which came first' a trick with a flat answer.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT one of the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
questions.rationale: The first trio was Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan and Raman. Nehru received it later, in 1955 — the odd-name-out version of the question.

questions.question: India's highest peacetime gallantry award is the:
questions.rationale: The Ashoka Chakra heads the peacetime ladder; the Param Vir Chakra is the wartime equivalent. The crossover between the two ladders is the exam's favourite swap.

questions.question: The first sportsperson to receive the Bharat Ratna was:
questions.rationale: Sachin Tendulkar received it in 2014, months after his retirement — the first sportsperson so honoured.

questions.question: Which award is India's highest literary honour?
questions.rationale: The Jnanpith Award (from 1965, first won by G. Sankara Kurup) tops the ladder; the Sahitya Akademi Award honours individual works in 24 languages.

questions.question: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is given for excellence in:
questions.rationale: It is Indian cinema's highest honour, instituted in 1969 — the centenary year of Dadasaheb Phalke — with Devika Rani the first recipient.

questions.question: The first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna was:
questions.rationale: Indira Gandhi received it in 1971. Lata Mangeshkar followed in 2001; Mother Teresa (1979) took the Nobel, not the first-woman Bharat Ratna slot.

questions.question: The Khel Ratna award was renamed in 2021 after which personality?
questions.rationale: It became the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2021, dropping the Rajiv Gandhi prefix. Older books carrying the old name are the trap's source.

questions.question: Which of these is a wartime gallantry award?
questions.rationale: The V-ladder (Param Vir, Maha Vir, Vir) is wartime; the Ashoka-Kirti-Shaurya series is peacetime. Vir Chakra is the only wartime name in the list.

questions.question: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize is associated with which field?
questions.rationale: CSIR's Bhatnagar Prize (from 1958) is India's highest science award, given to researchers under 45 — the age limit being a standard follow-up question.
